---
title: "Schedule"
---

::: {.callout-note}
Dates and times are placeholders — update once this year's schedule is
confirmed. The course is 1.5 days: a full Day 1, then a half-day
Day 2.
:::

## Day 1 (full day) — Scraping & Text Preprocessing

- What is Natural Language Processing (NLP)?
- Working with Wikipedia: pages, categories, revisions
- Web scraping: HTML tables, the Wikipedia API, and R wrappers
  (`WikipediR`, `wikkitidy`)
- Data preparation and cleaning
- Text preprocessing: tokenization, stopwords, stemming
- The document-feature matrix (DFM) and tf-idf weighting
- Descriptive analysis (word clouds, frequency plots)

[Slides](slides/day1.qmd) · [Notes](notes/day1.qmd)

## Day 2 (half day) — Supervised Learning, Word Embeddings & LLMs

- Supervised learning basics: train/test splits, class imbalance
- Dictionaries and Naive Bayes classification
- Model evaluation (accuracy, precision, recall, F1)
- Word embeddings (GloVe) and nearest-neighbor search
- Large language models (LLMs) and the transformer architecture
- Running local LLMs with Ollama

[Slides](slides/day2.qmd) · [Notes](notes/day2.qmd)

::: {.callout-tip}
Unsupervised learning / topic modeling (LDA) isn't covered in the
1.5-day format — see last year's material in `../IF/` if you want to
bring it back in for a longer run of the course.
:::
